segments.t: At the ASK agency, Gabriel suddenly realizes he made a catastrophic blunder with the casting names. He rushes to Andrea to explain that he reached Mathias's voicemail after confusing two candidates. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Andréa, on a un gros problème avec le casting.
Qu'est-ce qui se passe avec le film?
J'ai fait une énorme bêtise.
Bassem, ce n'est pas Baptiste.
Comment ça? Baptiste a quarante-cinq ans!
Oui, c'est un rôle très important.
C'est le partenaire principal de Gérard Lanvin.
Mais comment tu as pu confondre les deux?
Les deux prénoms se ressemblent trop.
Tu as essayé d'appeler Mathias?
Oui, je suis tombé sur sa messagerie.
Il faut trouver une solution tout de suite.
Je vais essayer de réparer mon erreur.
Dépêche-toi, le casting commence maintenant.
Let's explore the conversation line by line and unpack the French phrases.
Andréa, on a un gros problème avec le casting.
'Andrea, we have a big problem with the casting.' Gabriel breaks the bad news to Andrea. The masculine noun phrase 'un gros probleme' signals an urgent complication.
Qu'est-ce qui se passe avec le film?
'What is going on with the film?' Andrea asks what happened. The expression 'qu'est-ce qui se passe' inquires about the situation.
J'ai fait une énorme bêtise.
'I made a huge mistake.' Gabriel admits his serious blunder. The passe compose 'j'ai fait' expresses a completed past action.
Bassem, ce n'est pas Baptiste.
'Bassem is not Baptiste.' Gabriel explains the mix-up between two similar names. The negative structure 'ce n'est pas' corrects the mistaken identity.
Comment ça? Baptiste a quarante-cinq ans!
'What do you mean? Baptiste is forty-five years old!' Andrea reacts in shock. French expresses age using the verb 'avoir'.
Oui, c'est un rôle très important.
'Yes, it is a very important role.' Gabriel acknowledges the importance of the part. The adjective 'important' follows the masculine noun 'role'.
C'est le partenaire principal de Gérard Lanvin.
'He is the main partner of Gerard Lanvin.' Gabriel names the major movie star. The adjective 'principal' indicates the primary co-star role.
Mais comment tu as pu confondre les deux?
'But how could you confuse the two?' Andrea demands an explanation. The compound tense 'tu as pu' questions his decision-making.
Les deux prénoms se ressemblent trop.
'The two first names sound too much alike.' Gabriel explains the confusion. The reciprocal verb 'se ressembler' indicates mutual resemblance.
Tu as essayé d'appeler Mathias?
'Did you try calling Mathias?' Andrea asks whether Mathias was alerted. The infinitive 'appeler' follows the verb 'essayer de'.
Oui, je suis tombé sur sa messagerie.
'Yes, I reached his voicemail.' Gabriel explains that Mathias did not answer. The idiom 'tomber sur' means to end up at or encounter.
Il faut trouver une solution tout de suite.
'We must find a solution right away.' Andrea urges prompt action. The impersonal verb 'il faut' expresses strong necessity.
Je vais essayer de réparer mon erreur.
'I am going to try to fix my mistake.' Gabriel vows to make amends. The near future 'je vais essayer' announces his immediate effort.
Dépêche-toi, le casting commence maintenant.

'Hurry up, the casting is starting now.' Andrea gives urgent marching orders. The reflexive imperative 'depeche-toi' instructs someone to hurry. Now let's listen to the entire dialogue once more to lock in what you have learned.
